cities.d: (طرابلس) — the capital and largest city of Libya. The traveller's main entry point.

x.around: The best way to see Tripoli is to walk, there are plenty of great guides out there (books) to help you out and also you may come across some half-useful Libyan versions. The people are friendly and very inquisitive. But be aware if you're a westerner, or stick out like a sore thumb compared to a local. Don't walk around at night alone. Taxis are also useful but can be pricey for westerners.

n.en: Anglican Church of Christ The King

x.intro: Tripoli (Arabic: طرابلس, Tarabulus) is the capital, largest city, principal harbour and biggest commercial and manufacturing centre of the North African country of Libya. Tripoli is in the north-west of Libya on the Mediterranean Sea.

must.d: Formerly known as Green Square. This is a popular gathering place. It gives some good views of the old city walls. Some of the shopping streets also start here.
The national museum of Libya, covering 5,000 years of history in a vast palace complex with numerous courtyards which dominates the city skyline and is on the outskirts of the medina.
Only surviving Roman monument in the city.

next.d: are worth visiting. Sabratha is towards west of Tripoli and Leptis is to the east.

x.safe: Women may choose to dress modestly: long sleeves and long skirts or pants are considered most appropriate when shopping or sightseeing. Libya is not a conservative Muslim country, so head scarves are not necessary.

cities.d: (بنغازي) — the largest city of Cyrenaica and the second largest of the country

x.around: Taxis in Libya are interesting. They are either minibuses that travel round a predefined route or black and white cars (dead pandas) with taxi signs. Stick with the cars. Taxi travel is very cheap, but the vehicles are generally in a bad state of repair. Try to sit in the back as the journeys can be somewhat exciting when in the passenger seat, when drivers tend to turn across traffic lanes.
x.intro: Benghazi is the second largest city in Libya, with a population of 630,000 (2011). It is a center of Libyan commerce, industry, transport and culture. It continues to hold institutions and organizations normally associated with a capital city, including several national government buildings as well as the National Library of Libya.

must.d: Constructed during the 1930s in a neo-classical style, the Benghazi Cathedral used to be one of the largest churches in North Africa. It fell into disuse during the 1960s but has been renovated.

cities.d: (غدامس) — an oasis town with a large Berber population. The old part of the town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

x.intro: Ghadamis also known as Ghadames is an oasis town in Libya. The old part of the town is inscribed on UNESCO World Heritage List.

cities.d: (سبها) — an oasis city approximately 640 km (400 mi) south of Tripoli

x.around: There are also flights to Turkey, Tunisia and Egypt from Sabha air port which is the main airport for the southern region . Sabha county consists of few districts; Hajara, Al Jadeed, Al Gurdah, Sokara, Al Mahdiya, Al Mansheya, Guaeed and Al Thanawiya. It is surrounded by few urban districts and they are; Tamanhint, Samnu, Al Zegen, Goudwa
x.intro: Sabha is the capital of the municipality by the same name in Libya. It was once the capital of the ancient Fezzan region.
x.safe: See the warning on the Libya article for information on the security situation.

cities.d: (شحات) — Ancient city of Cyrene, a World Heritage site, is nearby

x.intro: Shahhat (Arabic: شحات) is a town in northeastern Libya, on the Mediterranean coast. It is the birthplace of St. Mark the Evangelist.

must.d: An ancient city started as a Greek colony. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

cities.d: (سِرْت) — the birthplace of Muammar Gaddafi, Libya's longtime ruler.

x.intro: Surt (also Sirt, Sirte) is a city in Libya, best known as Muammar Gaddhafi's hometown. Prior to the civil war of 2011 it was bestowed with a number of governmental edifices subsequently destroyed by NATO aerial bombardment, relentless shelling by NTC rebel forces and then subjected to vandalism and looting of the remains following the killing of Muammar Gaddhafi and the suspension of combative activities on 21 October 2011.
x.safe: See the warning on the Libya article for information on the security situation.

cities.d: (طبرق) — harbour town with World War II cemeteries

hidden.d: Commemorates soldiers killed during the Siege of Tobruk in 1941; see World War II in Africa.

x.intro: Tobruk (Arabic: طبرق‎, Tubruq) is a port city in the north-east of Libya.
x.safe: See the warning on the Libya article for information on the security situation.

intro: Libya (Arabic: ‏ليبيا, Libiya) is a country in the Maghreb region of North Africa and a part of the Arab world. Although the country is rich in history and culture and has great tourism potential, the country has been in the news for all the wrong reasons since the 1960s. Since the 2010s, the country has been in a state of flux and is rather dangerous to travel to.

other.d: small former Bedouin village on a wonderful oasis, around 150 km west of Sabha

x.around: The oasis, this is why it's famous. The village is not fully inhabited any more, but the tickle of tourists that do get to this place are met usually by some locals who sell accommodation for the night, tea and some local hand made souvenirs.
x.intro: Gaberoun is a small former Bedouin village on a wonderful oasis, around 150 km west of Sabha in the North African country of Libya.
x.safe: Be careful with local animals, sand snakes are common and can be found in shaded areas, but an altercation is rare.

other.d: an ancient settlement in the south west with prehistoric rock paintings and very challenging desert trekking

x.around: The town itself is small enough to move around on foot; sites outside of it are numerous and can be accessible by 4x4 vehicles.

must.d: First constructed by the Turks in early 20th century. It was completed by the Italians.

x.intro: Leptis Magna, also spelled Lepcis Magna, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa in the Tripolitania region of Libya.
